text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Attorney-General Amos Wako confirms that FORD-Kenya faction leader Raila Odinga and two senior officials of his faction submitted applications to the Registrar of Societies seeking registration as officials of the Labour Party of Kenya.
- A salary survey by Price Waterhouse reveals that the highest paid chief executive in Kenya gets a salary of 1.3 million shillings a month.
- An 18 year-old bride is recovering in hospital after her husband slashed off her left buttock with a panga in a savage attack.

- President Daniel arap Moi denies claims that his recent visit to London was aimed at challenging possible British support for President Yoweri Museveni of Uganda over the current Great Lakes crisis.
- An acute shortage of clean coffee has forced the Coffee Board of Kenya to suspend business for this week.

- Kenya Human Rights Commission has called on the Attorney-General, Amos Wako, to issue a public statement on the president's directive to the Chief Justice to keep political parties' disputes out of court.
- An unknown number of gangsters raid the chief's camp in Kiambu's Kikuyu area and escape with the entire security armoury.
